newsitem.title: USA: Chicago developer plans $750 mln complex downtown.
newsitem.headline: Chicago developer plans $750 mln complex downtown.

text.p: Chicago developer Daniel McLean unveiled plans Tuesday for a $750 million residential, commercial and retail complex in a rapidly growing neighborhood near downtown.
The "River East" development proposal includes construction of three condominium buildings and two large apartment houses in the first five years, said McLean, president of MCL Companies.
"It will probably end up being close to a $1 billion development when it gets done in the next 10 years and it certainly is one of the largest developments in the country," McLean said.
"It is the biggest contiguous property available in the downtown," McLean added. "There are bigger pieces in the south Loop, but the developments there aren't as big as these are."

Construction on the first phase is expected to begin in the fall with the development eventually including a 34-screen cinema, 400-room hotel, tree-lined walkways, a park and 4,000 parking spaces for an estimated 7,000 residents, McLean said.
McLean needs city planning department approval and will use mostly private financing, he said.
Residential spaces will overlook the Chicago River near its confluence with Lake Michigan. The development also includes North Pier and reacquisition of the city-occupied Kraft Building.

MCL affiliate Cityfront Center LLC acquired the 13-acre parcel after winning a bidding war for Chicago Dock & Canal Trust. The trust also owned the land under the Kraft Building, which city offices are due to vacate within a year.
McLean said about $8 million of infrastructure improvements will be needed, but the bulk of water and sewer needs have been completed over the past 10 years.
LaSalle National Bank has provided acquisition financing for the development with assistance from First National Bank Chicago, McLean said.

Chicago-based DeStefano and Partners is designing the luxury condominiums and Wheeler-Kearns Architecture will design walkways linking the new development with Michigan Avenue retailers and Navy Pier.
